title: Policy
summary: A rule that maps the current information state to an action and can be reapplied after future observations.
discover: An action is what you do now. A policy is the rule you keep using as observations change what you know.
engineer: Represent policies separately from one-shot recommendations so later actions can depend on updated belief rather than a frozen action list.
research: Use classical POMDP policy semantics; do not infer MMALS planning from routing alone.
evidence: Imported foundational concept from Kaelbling, Littman & Cassandra (1998).
limits: A policy can still be wrong when the model, objective or available actions are wrong.

title: Value and action value
summary: Expected multi-step value of a policy or of taking one action first and then continuing.
discover: Immediate reward can disagree with multi-step value when consequences arrive later.
engineer: Declare horizon, objective and uncertainty model before comparing plans.
research: Value is model- and objective-relative; it is not observed ground truth for one trajectory.
evidence: Imported foundational concept from POMDP planning literature.
limits: Longer horizons increase model dependence and computation.

title: Epistemic action
summary: An action chosen partly for what it can reveal and how that information can change later choices.
discover: Sometimes you act to learn what to do rather than to finish immediately.
engineer: Model evidence actions with explicit cost and with observation-dependent downstream decisions.
research: Information gain alone is not value of information.
evidence: Grounded in classical partially observable planning.
limits: A probe can reduce uncertainty while having zero or negative decision value.

title: Value of information
summary: Expected improvement in decision value enabled by information, net of acquisition cost or delay.
discover: More certainty is useful only when it helps choose better enough to justify the cost of learning.
engineer: Separate confidence/entropy metrics from the effect of evidence on downstream decisions.
research: GO-ED-POMDP relevance is project-specific; no general superiority claim follows.
evidence: Foundational mechanism grounded in partially observable planning; project applications remain empirical questions.
limits: Its value depends on the goal, action set, horizon and cost model.

title: Contingent policy
summary: A plan whose later actions branch according to observations not yet seen.
discover: Plan a rule for future branches instead of pretending future evidence is already known.
engineer: Keep observation branches explicit enough that tests can verify the decision path.
research: A contingent policy need not be materialized as an infinite explicit tree.
limits: Policy quality still depends on the transition/observation model and objective.

title: Receding-horizon planning
summary: Plan a bounded future, execute one step, observe, update, then plan again.
discover: Think ahead without pretending the first plan must survive future evidence unchanged.
engineer: Use bounded planning plus repeated state estimation when a full policy tree is computationally impractical.
research: The pattern is not evidence that MMALS already implements model-predictive control.
evidence: General planning/control concept; Diderot uses it pedagogically.
limits: A short horizon can miss delayed consequences; a long horizon can amplify model error and cost.

title: Predictive state representation
summary: Represent state through action-conditioned predictions of future observable tests rather than named hidden-state coordinates.
discover: A useful state coordinate can describe what future experiments are predicted to reveal.
engineer: Do not treat an arbitrary one-step prediction vector as a sufficient PSR without update/prediction sufficiency tests.
research: Exact predictive coordinates, estimated coordinates and learned next-observation features are different evidence classes.
limits: Sufficient predictive tests and learnability are separate questions.

title: Decision regret
summary: Expected value lost when decisions use a representation or policy instead of a declared reference.
discover: Prediction error and decision harm are not the same quantity.
engineer: Declare reference, horizon, objective and action set before interpreting regret.
research: Zero regret is evidence only for the declared decision query, not complete world-state reconstruction.
evidence: Used as an operational metric in the separate Toy A/F program; this wiki entry is pedagogical.
limits: A representation can have zero regret for one query and fail another.

title: Contingent sufficiency
summary: Project-local hypothesis that a compact state should preserve relevant adaptive future decision value, not only today's action.
discover: Two histories can agree on today's action yet support different future observation-dependent plans.
engineer: Specify goal, horizon, actions, costs, observations and policy class before claiming sufficiency.
research: This wording must be compared against state-abstraction, bisimulation and predictive-state literature before broader use.
evidence: Hypothesis only; separate Toy F2 is preregistered but not qualified/reviewed.
limits: Not a field definition of sufficient statistic or world-model state.

title: Belief ≠ model ≠ memory
summary: Separate current uncertainty, learned dynamics/inference structure, and durable evidence or competence memory.
discover: What I believe now, how I think the system evolves, and what I refuse to forget without evidence are different objects.
engineer: Allow beliefs to update while applying independent protection/governance to validated competence, constraints and provenance.
research: Conceptual separation does not require three physically separate tensors or modules.
evidence: Project synthesis informed by POMDP state estimation and continual-learning concerns.
limits: Requires system-specific semantics before implementation claims.

title: Non-regression evidence
summary: Finite replay or sentinels give bounded evidence of retained competence; they do not generally prove global invariance.
discover: Checking old cases is not the same as proving the new model cannot fail anywhere else.
engineer: State coverage and assumptions for sentinel tests; use structural isolation or mathematical bounds when stronger guarantees are required.
research: MMALS non-regression remains an experimental objective, not a universal guarantee.
evidence: Grounded in continual-learning assurance concerns; no global proof claimed.
limits: Strength depends on coverage and model structure.
